D-estimates of the average treatment effect (ATE) are consistent under the selection on observables assumption and that D-estimator are asymptotically normally distributed under the same assumption.

(1) the D-estimators are consistent estimators of the average treatment effect in the target population; and (2) D-estimators can be computed using only data from the treated sample and the control sample (i.e., without using any data on the outcome variable in the target population).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: What is a good way to use a control group to estimate the impact of a treatment?
the problem of estimating causal effects in non-experimental settings, where random assignment is not available.
developing a statistical framework to estimate the average impact of a program or intervention in a population of interest, and to assess the reliability of the resulting estimates.

D-estimates can be used in the presence of unobserved heterogeneity if the \strongly ignorability" condition is met.
D-estimation is a consistent method of estimation of causal effects in the presence of selection bias, provided that the \strongly ignorability" assumption holds.
D-estimation is the best available method for nonparametric estimation of average treatment effects in observational studies.

D-estimator is a consistent estimator of the average impact of a treatment on a target population under the strongly ignorable treatment assumption.

The main takeaway from our work is that
D-estimation is a viable alternative to regression adjustment and matching methods in the presence of a large number of covariates.
